title: Reconstruct Adam
summary: Build Adam from exponential gradient moments through bias correction and a complete parameter update.

parts.title: Two moving averages
parts.prompt: What different information is captured by Adam's first and second moments?
parts.answer: The first moment is an exponential average of gradients and tracks direction. The second moment averages squared gradients and tracks coordinate-wise scale, reducing steps in consistently high-variance directions.
hints: One tracks signed values; one tracks magnitudes.

parts.title: Why bias correction?
parts.prompt: Why are m and v divided by 1-b1^t and 1-b2^t?
parts.answer: Both accumulators start at zero, so early moving averages are biased toward zero. Dividing by the missing accumulated weight produces corrected estimates, especially important in the first steps.
hints: Evaluate the first update from zero.
The correction approaches one as t grows.

parts.title: Role of epsilon
parts.prompt: Where is epsilon placed in Adam and what failure does it prevent?
parts.answer: Epsilon is added to the denominator after the square root. It prevents division by zero and limits numerical instability when the estimated second moment is tiny.
hints: Consider a coordinate whose gradients are always zero.
Epsilon is a numerical safeguard, not a learning-rate substitute.

parts.title: Update Adam moments
parts.prompt: Implement the exponential first- and second-moment updates.

parts.title: Implement one Adam step
parts.prompt: Update moments, apply bias correction, and return the new parameter and moment tensors.
